entries: Friction opposes relative motion: a 60-newton push drives the block right, a 40-newton friction arrow grows at the contact against the slide, and the net 20 newtons to the right keeps the block sliding.
slots.label: Friction
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Moments: 60 newtons at 0.5 metres makes 30 newton-metres on the left; 30 newtons at 0.75 metres makes only 22.5 on the right, so the beam tips - then the right weight slides to 1.0 metre, its moment rises to 30, and the beam balances.
slots.label: Moments
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Pressure: a 200-newton crate on a 0.5-square-metre face gives 400 pascals; tipped onto a 0.05-square-metre edge the same force gives 4000 pascals - one tenth the area, ten times the pressure.
slots.label: Pressure
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Check the thinking: the driving wheel pushes backward on the road at its contact patch, so friction pushes the car forward - friction opposes the relative slide, not the motion.
slots.label: Check the thinking
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The force between two surfaces in contact that opposes their relative slide - which is why it can point forward on a driving wheel.
slots.label: Friction
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The single force left after opposing forces are combined: a 60 N push against 40 N of friction leaves a net 20 N.
slots.label: Net force
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The turning effect of a force, calculated as force times distance from the pivot, measured in newton-metres.
slots.label: Moment
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The fixed point a beam or lever turns around; every moment distance is measured from it.
slots.label: Pivot
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Force spread over an area, calculated as force divided by area, measured in pascals.
slots.label: Pressure
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The unit of pressure: one pascal is one newton spread over one square metre.
slots.label: Pascal
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
